questions: Q1: Does the CLI playbook command group follow the existing goals/ pattern?
Q2: Does the check command implement POST trigger + GET polling with correct intervals?
Q3: Does the checks command list history with formatted output and --json support?
Q4: Is the playbook case correctly registered in the main dispatcher?

answers.answer: Yes. src/playbook/index.ts follows the goals/index.ts pattern exactly: switch-based subcommand dispatch, help text, parseApiError error handling, isHelpRequested checks.
evidence: src/playbook/index.ts uses same structure as src/goals/index.ts

answers.answer: Yes. cmdPlaybookCheck in check.ts: POST to /playbook/rules/${ruleId}/check with basePath: '/api', then polls GET every 5 seconds (POLL_INTERVAL_MS=5000) for up to 120 iterations (MAX_POLLS=120, 10 minutes). Terminal states: PASS, FAIL, ERROR. Supports --json. Exit code 0 for PASS, 1 otherwise.

Yes. cmdPlaybookChecks in checks.ts: GET /playbook/rules/${ruleId}/checks with basePath: '/api'. Displays formatted table with ID, Status, Compliance Rate, Checked At. Handles empty list. Supports --json.
evidence: checks.ts formats output with padEnd alignment
checks.ts handles empty checks array with 'No checks found' message

answers.answer: Yes. src/index.ts has import for runPlaybook and a 'playbook' case in the switch statement using configOrHelp pattern. Usage text updated with playbook commands.

statement: CLI implementation complete. 4 files changed (3 new, 1 modified). Playbook command group with check (trigger+poll) and checks (history list) subcommands. TypeScript compiles clean. CHK-03 and CHK-04 blocked by staging server not having new endpoints deployed.
